user.title: Add a Road.io charger
user.description: How do you want to find the charger?

menu_options.manual: I already have a Location ID

search.title: Where do you want to charge?
search.description: Type an address or place and press Submit to move the map there, or move the pin yourself. Drag the circle to set how far to search (up to {max_radius} m). Addresses are looked up via [© OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright).

data_description.address: Your home location is already on the map, no need to type it.

search_found.title: Is this the right spot?
search_found.description:
📍 Found: **{place}**

Press Submit to search for chargers around the pin. You can still move the pin, resize the circle or type another address. Address lookup via [© OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright).

pick.title: Choose a charger
pick.description: Found {count} charger(s), closest first. Chargers you've already added aren't listed.

data_description.name: Leave empty to use the address.

manual.title: Enter a Location ID
manual.description: Give the charger a name and enter its Location ID.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the Road.io API. Try again later.
error.invalid_location: Road.io does not know this Location ID.
error.unknown: Unexpected error, check the Home Assistant logs.
error.no_chargers: No Road.io chargers found in this area. Try a larger circle or another spot.
error.all_added: All chargers in this area have already been added.
error.geocode_failed: Couldn't look up the address at OpenStreetMap. Try again later or move the pin yourself.
error.address_not_found: Address not found. Try writing it differently, for example with the town name.

abort.already_configured: This charging location has already been added.

init.title: Charge wish notifications
init.description: Turn on the bell (Laadwens) on the card or the switch and you'll get a notification as soon as a socket at this charger is free. Settings are copied from your previous charger when you add a new one.

data.disarm_after_notify: Turn the charge wish off after notifying
data.notify_when_taken: Notify if it's taken again before you arrive
data.person: Person (to recognise that you took the charger yourself)
data.expire_hours: Turn the charge wish off automatically after
data.min_free_minutes: Only notify when free for at least

data_description.notify_targets: Phones with the Home Assistant app, or the notification area in Home Assistant itself.
data_description.notify_when_taken: Applies for 30 minutes after a 'free' notification.
data_description.person: If this person is within 200 m when the charger becomes taken, it's you: no 'taken again' notification, and the charge wish turns off.
data_description.min_free_minutes: Prevents false alarms when a socket is only briefly free. 0 = notify straight away.
